term.name: Steganography
term.short: Steganography conceals the existence of a payload by embedding it in an ordinary-looking cover medium.
term.meta_title: Steganography — Definition, Methods, and Limits | CiphersOnline
term.meta_description: Learn how hidden data is embedded in text, images, or audio, how steganography differs from encryption, and how detection or editing can expose it.

body.title: Definition and methods
body.html: Steganography places a payload inside a cover such as text, an image, or audio so that communication is less noticeable. Methods include selected letters in prose, subtle pixel changes, and modifications to transform coefficients or file structure.

body.title: Steganography and encryption
body.html: Encryption hides meaning but usually leaves visible ciphertext; steganography aims to hide that a payload exists. The two can be combined. Security depends on the embedding method, key, cover quality, and adversary, while resizing, compression, or statistical analysis may destroy or reveal hidden data.

faq.question: Is steganography encryption?
faq.answer: No. It conceals presence rather than necessarily transforming meaning, though the payload may be encrypted first.

faq.question: Can hidden data survive editing?
faq.answer: Only if the method is robust to the particular edit; recompression, cropping, or format conversion often damages fragile payloads.
